extracted.intended_audience: general readers, public-relations students and practitioners seeking an overview of PR principles and ethics
extracted.subtask_description: A broad encyclopedic overview of public relations practice, covering disciplines, tactics (including press releases), audience segmentation, measurement, crisis communication, and professional ethical standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA — Advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy: Serving the public interest by acting as responsible advocates for the clientele.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display the marketplace of ideas, facts and viewpoints to aid informed public debate; balance advocacy for clients with consideration of the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA — Honesty
rubrics_metrics.description: Honesty: Standing by the truth and accuracy of all facts in the case and advancing those statements to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fact-check and present accurate information to maintain credibility with employers, clients, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA — Expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Expertise: To become and stay informed of the specialized knowledge needed in the field of Public Relations; improve the field through development, research and education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional knowledge, develop credibility and relationships to understand audiences and industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA — Independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Independence: Provide unbiased work to those that are represented while being accountable for all actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain professional judgment and be transparent about conflicts of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA — Loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Loyalty: Stay devoted to the client while remembering that there is a duty to still serve the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance client advocacy with obligations to the broader public good.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA — Fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Fairness: Honorably conduct business with any and all clients, employers, competitors, peers, vendors, media and general public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect all opinions and the right of free expression; avoid discriminatory or exploitative practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: IABC Code principles (international ethics guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: IABC members follow principles including having proper and legal communication, openness to other cultures, creating accurate and trustworthy communication, being credible and honest, keeping information accurate, respecting free speech, obeying policies and laws, giving proper credit, and protecting private information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these principles when communicating internationally: ensure legality, cultural sensitivity, accuracy, respect for free speech, proper attribution, data/privacy protection, and avoidance of unethical behaviors or accepting gifts for coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: TARES — Truthfulness (of the message)
rubrics_metrics.description: Truthfulness: Is this communicating something factually true and accurate? Does this downplay or diminish evidence? Am I creating a false narrative or image?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the TARES test question prompts from the article to evaluate whether a persuasive message is factually accurate and not misleading.

rubrics_metrics.name: TARES — Authenticity (of the persuader)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authenticity: Will people question my honesty or integrity? Do I truly believe what is being presented will benefit the audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the persuader authentically supports the claims and whether the persuader's integrity will be questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: TARES — Respect (for the persuadee)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect: Am I presenting statements in self-interest, or do I genuinely care about the issue or audience? Is this presented to rational, self-thinking beings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider ethical responsibility toward the audience and whether the communication treats persuadees with dignity and respect.

rubrics_metrics.name: TARES — Equity (of the persuasive appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Equity: Is this appeal fair and nondiscriminatory? Have I targeted persuadees who are not capable of understanding the claims and context?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate fairness across audiences; avoid exploiting vulnerable groups or misrepresenting information to those unable to evaluate claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: TARES — Social responsibility (for the common good)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social responsibility: Will my statements cause harm to groups? Have I fairly presented issues concerning underrepresented groups? Are communications responsible to societal groups and the public interest?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge persuasive communications for broader societal consequences and obligations to the public good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online PR measurement — Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement: Measure the number of people who engaged with an item (social shares, likes and comments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track likes, shares, comments and other interaction metrics to evaluate how audiences respond to online content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online PR measurement — Impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Impressions: Measure the number of people who may have viewed an item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use impressions to estimate potential exposure; understand it counts potential views, not necessarily unique engaged users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online PR measurement — Items
rubrics_metrics.description: Items: Measure any content (blog posts, articles, etc.) that originally appeared as digital media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count and catalog original content produced or distributed as part of a campaign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online PR measurement — Mentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions: Measure how many online items mention the brand, organization, or product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track earned mentions across media to assess coverage and sentiment where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online PR measurement — Reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Reach: Measure how far the PR campaign managed to penetrate overall and in terms of a particular audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reach to understand audience breadth and campaign penetration into target segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience targeting and segmentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify target audience(s) and tailor messages relevant to each audience; sometimes create several distinct but complementary messages while keeping consistency in overall theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand needs and desires of each segment; create messages relevant to each; ensure messages are consistent with one another to avoid contradiction and maintain coherent themes across stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Messaging consistency and storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Messaging: create a consistent story around a product, person, company, or service to prevent contradictory or confusing information that could instill doubt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop an overarching problem statement, industry viewpoint or brand perception to be shared across sources and media; align spokespeople and materials to the same narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis preparation and risk management
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation for crisis management includes risk management: identification and mitigation of potential risks before they occur and development of crisis communication plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans should identify spokespersons, establish communication protocols, and include staff training and scenario planning to be ready for potential crises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis response — timeliness and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: During a crisis, timely and transparent communication is vital; disseminate accurate information to the public, stakeholders, and the media, addressing concerns and correcting misinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act quickly, be transparent about what is known/unknown, coordinate with media relations and stakeholder engagement to ensure accurate reporting and mitigate harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-crisis recovery and learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-crisis PR focuses on rebuilding the organization's image and learning from the event to improve future responses; part of reputation management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct post-mortems, implement improvements to processes and communications, and engage in sustained reputation rebuilding activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publics classification (segmentation types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publics can be classified as Traditional, Non-Traditional, Latent, Aware, Intervening, Primary, Secondary, Internal, External, Domestic, and International.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories to map stakeholders and decide communication approaches, being mindful of cultural differences for international publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publics development stages (Grunig)
rubrics_metrics.description: Publics develop in stages: Non-Publics, Latent Publics, Apathetic Publics, Aware Publics, Active Publics, determined by problem recognition, constraint recognition and involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess what stage each public is in to tailor messaging and activation strategies appropriately (e.g., awareness-building vs. mobilization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Media relations: Building and maintaining close relationships with news media so they can fairly and accurately report on an organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop and maintain media contacts and directories (editors, deadlines, types of contributions); leverage relationships and tailor pitches by outlet type, industry and publication frequency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social media use and interactive PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Social media marketing: publish content on social media profiles, engage with followers, analyze results, and run social ads to build brands, increase sales, and drive website traffic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce shareable content, engage authentically with audiences, monitor analytics and adjust strategies; incorporate social platforms as extensions of traditional PR tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid spin and manipulative tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Spin refers to providing a certain interpretation of information meant to sway public opinion; historically linked to deceit but now often described as polishing the truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid manipulative techniques (cherry picking, non-denial denials, euphemisms, ambiguity, timing to exploit news events). Skilled 'spin' undermines trust; ethical PR aims to earn trust and goodwill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition and risks of negative/black-hat PR and reputation laundering
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative public relations (black hat PR, reputation laundering): processes intended to destroy a target's reputation or conceal unethical/criminal behavior, often using fake accounts, misleading facts, or front groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize these as unethical practices that damage public discourse and can create legal and reputational risks; avoid participation and be alert to such tactics in competitors or vendors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-checking, accuracy, attribution and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: PR professionals must ensure proper information, fact-checking, accurate communication, proper credit to resources, and protection of private information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain credibility by verifying facts, attributing sources, obeying laws and policies regarding confidential information, and refusing gifts or payments that compromise independence or ethics.
